key_insight: HyCOP learns a small, interpretable policy that composes simple modules (advection, diffusion, learned closures, boundary handling) into short programs to form parametric PDE solution operators, enabling accurate, query-conditioned predictions without a monolithic black box.
problem_solved: Reduces brittleness and opacity of monolithic operator-learning surrogates by providing a modular, interpretable, and query-time-flexible framework that adapts to different regimes and timesteps.
method: Decompose PDE solution operator into reusable modules (numerical sub-solvers and learned components) for advection, diffusion, closures, and boundary handling.
Learn a policy that, conditioned on regime features and state statistics, selects which module to apply and for how long—effectively assembling short programs instead of a single end-to-end map.
Evaluate composed hybrid surrogates at arbitrary query times, enabling fast, interpretable, and regime-aware prediction.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a practical path to accurate, physically interpretable surrogate models for PDEs that generalize across regimes and query times, combining numerical reliability with learned flexibility.
visual_elements: Modular architecture diagram: modules (advection, diffusion, closure, boundary) as blocks with a policy controller assembling them into short programs.
Timeline / program composition graphic: sequence of applied modules and durations vs a single monolithic mapping, showing interpretability and temporal flexibility.
Performance comparison chart: ground truth vs HyCOP vs monolithic surrogate across multiple query times and regimes (error bars or heatmaps).
Policy visualization: regime-feature input to a decision map (e.g., colored policy probabilities) illustrating which modules are chosen in different physical regimes.
paper_title: HyCOP: Hybrid Composition Operators for Interpretable Learning of PDEs
paper_authors: Jinpai Zhao, Nishant Panda, Yen Ting Lin, Eirik Valseth, Diane Oyen
